'''Susuki Mizu Shrine''' (須須岐水神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[Chikuma City]], {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}. It is identified as the {{ill|Shikigesha|ja|式外社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikigesha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Susuki Mizu Shrine, with its {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=this used to link to modern system but that one is too overlinked|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}} classification as a former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== Overview ==

According to shrine tradition, it was founded in the second year of the [[Hakuhō era]] (673 CE). Initially known as {{ill|Hōri Shrine|ja|祝神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōri Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, it later enshrined {{ill|Sannō Gongen|ja|山王権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sannō Gongen|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} from {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi Taisha|qid=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Taisha}} at the behest of {{ill|Kanasashi Toneri Masanaga|ja|金刺舎人正長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanasashi Toneri Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a {{ill|Gunji|ja|郡司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gunji}} of {{ill|Hanishina District, Nagano|en|Hanishina District, Nagano|qid=Q726661|lt=Hanishina District}}, after flooding from the {{ill|Shinano River|ja|千曲川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma River|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信濃川|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q734455}} during the {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan era}}. In later periods, it gained the patronage of the {{ill|Sanada clan|en|Sanada clan|qid=Q1002844|lt=Sanada clan}}, receiving land grants of 300 koku and festival contributions. 

Rebuilt in 1851 during the {{ill|Kaei|en|Kaei|qid=Q1146125|lt=Kaei era}} under the guidance of {{ill|Tatekawa Washirō Tomimasa|ja|立川和四郎富昌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatekawa Washirō Tomimasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the shrine was renamed from "Sannō Daigongen Palace" to "Susuki Mizu Shrine" by the {{ill|Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida clan}} in 1781 ({{ill|Tenmei|en|Tenmei|qid=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei}} 1). The shrine formerly held rituals involving the exchange of {{ill|Mikoshi|en|Mikoshi|qid=Q979940|lt=Mikoshi}} with {{ill|Amamiya Shrine|ja|雨宮の坐日吉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amamiya Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} but discontinued this in 1872 (Meiji 5).

The shrine grounds span approximately 27 ken (east to west) and 34 ken (north to south). Revered as a {{ill|Suijin|en|Suijin|qid=Q3137449|lt=water god}}, it has long served as the guardian deity of the Yashiro Irrigation Weir.

'''Susuki Mizu Shrine''' (須須岐水神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|en|Chikuma, Nagano|qid=Q179757|lt=Chikuma, Nagano}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}, Japan. It is associated with the ancient {{ill|Shikigesha|ja|式外社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines listed in Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikigesha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Susuki Mizu Shrine and held the status of a village shrine (旧郷社) under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=this used to link to modern system but that one is too overlinked|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}.

== Overview ==
According to shrine tradition, Susuki Mizu Shrine was founded in the second year of the {{ill|Hakuhō|ja|白鳳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakuhō period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11580612}} (673). Initially, it was known as the "Hōri Shrine" (祝神社), a name derived from the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}. During the {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)}} era, following flooding of the {{ill|Shinano River|ja|千曲川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma River|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信濃川|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q734455}}, the regional governor of {{ill|Hanishina District, Nagano|en|Hanishina District, Nagano|qid=Q726661|lt=Hanishina District}}, {{ill|Kanasashi no Masanaga|ja|金刺正長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanasashi no Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, brought the {{ill|Sannō Gongen|ja|山王権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sannō Gongen|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} from {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi Taisha|qid=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Taisha}} and enshrined it alongside the main deity.

In the Edo period, the shrine received the patronage of the {{ill|Sanada clan|en|Sanada clan|qid=Q1002844|lt=Sanada clan}}, who donated 300 koku of land and additional resources for rituals. The shrine was reconstructed by {{ill|Tatekawa Washirō Tomimasa|ja|立川和四郎富昌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatekawa Washirō Tomimasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in the fourth year of {{ill|Kaei|en|Kaei|qid=Q1146125|lt=Kaei}} (1851) following repeated flood damage. In the first year of {{ill|Tenmei|en|Tenmei|qid=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei}} (1781), the shrine was renamed "Susuki Mizu Shrine" by the head of Shinto priests, the {{ill|Urabe clan|ja|卜部氏|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Urabe_clan|fr|User:Immanuelle/Urabe_clan|lt=Yoshida clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Urabe clan}}.

Previously, the shrine participated in rituals involving the transfer of portable shrines (神輿) with {{ill|Amamiya Shrine|ja|雨宮の坐日吉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amamiya Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, but these were discontinued in the fifth year of {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} (1872).

The shrine site measures approximately 27 ken east-to-west and 34 ken north-to-south. It has been worshipped as a {{ill|Suijin|en|Suijin|qid=Q3137449|lt=water god}}, serving as the guardian of the Yashiro irrigation system.
